commit f1290fc2216a8c538b3bc095520547d109c1fccc
Author: Abhi Singh <abhi@entire.io>
Date:   Wed Oct 21 21:41:17 2026 +0530

    Cut Julia signatures at the header and stop module DATA_FLOWS
    
    tree-sitter-julia keeps body statements as direct, unlabeled children of
    function, macro, struct and module definitions, and a short-form
    definition is an assignment, so signatureFromNode never found a body
    boundary: every Julia signature carried the whole definition, and a
    module's carried every member. compareEntities checks the signature
    first, so a Julia body edit read as signature_changed on the function and
    again on its module; USES_TYPE turned types named in a body into edges;
    and parameterNames parsed the body into the parameter list, hiding
    parameter-forwarding flows.
    
    juliaSignature now ends the signature at the signature child (functions
    and macros, keeping ::ReturnType and where clauses), at type_head
    (structs), at the module name, or at the left-hand side of a short-form
    definition, keeps abstract/primitive headers whole, and leaves the
    generic signature in place when the child is missing. It is applied
    after entity construction like the F# override and recomputes the
    fingerprint.
    
    The DATA_FLOWS pass also scanned module symbols, whose block spans their
    members, so each member's return flows were emitted again with the
    module as the endpoint, in Julia and Ruby alike. It now skips modules in
    every language; call resolution never yields a module target, so no
    DATA_FLOWS record has a module at either end. callableSymbol is
    unchanged and still gates ASYNC_CALLS and the HTTP scan.
